title: Thinking About Moving to La Cañada? It’s District, District, District
author: lacanada.us editorial staff
image_alt: La Cañada Unified School District campus life
excerpt: In La Cañada Flintridge, the modern real-estate saying is district, district, district. LCUSD ranks at or near the top of California unified districts on CAASPP, and that is a big reason families pay a premium to live here.
body_markdown:
There’s an old real-estate saying: **location, location, location.**

In La Cañada Flintridge, you could make a strong case that the modern version is:

**district, district, district.**

If you’re considering moving to La Cañada, the public school district is one of the biggest reasons families are willing to pay a premium to live here.

La Cañada Unified School District — LCUSD — is small, academically intense, well-supported by the community, and currently performing at or near the very top of California’s public-school system.

And unlike a lot of “best schools” claims you see on real-estate listings, this one is backed up by state testing data.

## Start With the Numbers

According to California’s official **2024–25 CAASPP results**, the percentage of LCUSD students meeting or exceeding state standards was:

| Subject               | LCUSD students meeting or exceeding standard | Statewide rank among unified districts |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------: | -------------------------------------: |
| English Language Arts |                                      **89%** |                                 **#1** |
| Mathematics           |                                      **84%** |                                 **#2** |
| Science               |                                      **75%** |                                 **#1** |

That is an unusually strong academic profile.

In English Language Arts, **61%** of LCUSD students exceeded the state standard, while another **28%** met it. In mathematics, **63%** exceeded the standard and another **21%** met it.

Put simply:

**La Cañada ranked first in California in English, first in science, and second in math among unified school districts.**

For families moving into the Los Angeles area specifically because of public schools, that immediately puts LCUSD in a very short list of districts worth studying.

## How Does La Cañada Compare With the Rest of Los Angeles?

Los Angeles County has an enormous range of public-school options.

There is Los Angeles Unified, of course, but also a collection of smaller, highly regarded districts in communities such as Arcadia, South Pasadena, San Marino, Manhattan Beach, Palos Verdes and elsewhere.

La Cañada stands out even in that company.

Because LCUSD ranks **#1 statewide among unified districts in English Language Arts and science**, it also sits at the top of Los Angeles County unified districts in those subjects.

Its **#2 statewide mathematics ranking** puts it essentially one step from the top there as well.

For families relocating to greater Los Angeles who want a strong traditional public-school district, that is one of the clearest reasons La Cañada ends up on the shortlist.

## California Distinguished Schools

State test scores are not the only recognition LCUSD schools have received.

In **2023, all three La Cañada Unified elementary schools were named California Distinguished Schools**:

- **La Cañada Elementary**
- **Palm Crest Elementary**
- **Paradise Canyon Elementary**

The designation is awarded to individual schools rather than districts, and California rotates recognition cycles between elementary and secondary schools.

So it would be inaccurate to say LCUSD itself is a “Distinguished School district.”

But having all three elementary schools recognized in the same cycle says quite a bit about the consistency of the system.

For a family considering moving here, that may matter more than having one standout campus surrounded by average ones.

## Don't Live in La Cañada? There May Still Be a Path In

Here is something many families outside the area do not realize:

**You may not necessarily have to live within LCUSD boundaries to attend the district.**

LCUSD operates a non-resident permit program that includes an employment-based option commonly associated with California’s **Allen Bill** provisions.

Under the district’s current guidelines, a parent or legal guardian may be eligible to apply if they are physically employed within LCUSD boundaries:

- **32 or more hours per week** for the district’s full-time category
- **16 or more hours per week** for its part-time category

Applicants generally need to provide documentation such as an employer letter, a recent pay stub and student academic records.

This is particularly relevant to families connected with one of La Cañada’s best-known employers: **NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory**.

JPL employees have historically used employment-based permits to enroll children in LCUSD, and the district has conducted permit outreach specifically for JPL employees.

That can make La Cañada schools an option for some families who work here but live elsewhere.

There are a few important caveats.

**A permit is not guaranteed.**

Residents receive priority, and non-resident students are admitted only when the district determines that space is available. LCUSD uses a priority and lottery system rather than simply accepting every applicant.

The district also offers several other permit categories, including provisions involving district employees, siblings of existing permit students and certain legacy circumstances.

If you think you may qualify, start with the **Non-Resident Permit Applications** section of the official LCUSD website. The rules and annual application dates can change, so treat any summary — including this one — as an introduction rather than the final word.

## One Reason the Schools Stay Strong: The Community Helps Pay for Them

Families moving here should also know about the **La Cañada Flintridge Educational Foundation — LCFEF**.

LCFEF is a major private funding source for the district and raises millions of dollars to support programs that many parents might otherwise assume are simply part of the regular school budget.

Foundation funding helps support areas such as:

- smaller class sizes
- counselors
- technology
- music and arts
- instructional programs
- teacher staffing and salaries

LCFEF reported raising about **$2.7 million for LCUSD in 2024–25**, and the Foundation says its 2025–26 campaign will provide approximately **$2.2 million for the 2026–27 school year**.

For **2026–27, LCFEF is requesting a contribution of $3,500 per family**.

It is voluntary.

Not every household can or should feel obligated to give that amount.

But if you move here and can comfortably afford the requested contribution, it is worth considering giving the full amount.

One of the reasons families choose La Cañada is the quality of the schools, and one of the reasons those schools can provide programs beyond basic state funding is that local families consistently support them.

In other words, the community does not just benefit from strong schools.

It invests in keeping them strong.

## What This Means If You're Considering a Move

No school district is perfect.

And test scores alone should never determine whether a community is right for your family.

But if public education is a major factor in your move, La Cañada deserves serious consideration.

The numbers are unusually strong:

- **89% of LCUSD students meet or exceed the ELA standard**
- **84% meet or exceed the mathematics standard**
- **75% meet or exceed the science standard**
- **#1 among California unified districts in English**
- **#1 in science**
- **#2 in mathematics**
- **All three elementary schools were named California Distinguished Schools in 2023**

Add in a small district, substantial community financial support, and a permit program that can create opportunities for some families working locally, and you begin to understand why the school district plays such an outsized role in La Cañada real estate.

In La Cañada, it may still be location, location, location.

But for families with children?

**It’s district, district, district.**

*(Curious about who's #1 in math? Here's your clue: the district shares its name with a nearby city whose name is almost identical to that of one of Europe's tiniest countries.)*
